questions.question: What does `students.Max(s => s.Score)` return, vs `students.Max()`?
options: Max(s => s.Score) returns the largest Score value; Max() alone would fail to compile since Student has no natural ordering
Max(s => s.Score) returns the whole Student object with the largest score
Max() returns a list of all maximum values
questions.explanation: The selector lambda tells LINQ WHICH value to compare across objects. Without it, `Max()` doesn't know how to compare two Student objects, and Student doesn't implement IComparable — it won't compile.

questions.question: What's the difference between `First(predicate)` and `FirstOrDefault(predicate)` when nothing matches?
options: First throws InvalidOperationException; FirstOrDefault returns a safe default (0/null/false) instead
FirstOrDefault is slower but otherwise identical
questions.explanation: Same philosophy as int.Parse vs TryParse — First is for 'this MUST exist or something is badly wrong'; FirstOrDefault is for when 'not found' is a normal, expected outcome you'll check for.

questions.question: What prints?
questions.explanation: Any() is true if AT LEAST ONE matches (22 > 20 — true). All() requires EVERY element to match (4 and 9 don't — false).

questions.question: What does `.OrderByDescending(s => s.Score).ThenBy(s => s.Name)` do?
options: Sorts by Name only, ignoring Score
Sorts by Score descending; when two students have the SAME Score, breaks the tie by Name ascending
Sorts by Score, then re-sorts the whole thing by Name, discarding the Score order
It's invalid — you can't chain OrderBy with ThenBy
questions.explanation: ThenBy is a SECONDARY sort key, only applied to break ties left over from the primary OrderBy/OrderByDescending. Elements with different Scores are unaffected by the ThenBy.

questions.question: After `var groups = students.GroupBy(s => s.Grade);`, what does each element of `groups` contain?
options: A `.Key` (the grade) plus all the Student objects that share that grade — itself enumerable
questions.explanation: Each group from GroupBy has a `.Key` property (the value the lambda returned) and is itself an IEnumerable<T> of every element that shared that key — you can foreach, Select, Count, etc. on it.

questions.question: How do you get 'page 2' of results, 10 per page (i.e., results 11-20)?
questions.explanation: Skip(10) discards the first 10 (page 1), then Take(10) keeps the next 10 (page 2's worth). Order matters: Take before Skip would give a different, usually wrong, result.
